speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I see you are experiencing a chronic cough, weight loss, and generalized weakness; to begin my assessment, have you noticed any night sweats or hemoptysis (coughing up blood) in addition to these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; given your recent release from prison and these "B symptoms" (fever, night sweats, weight loss), have you experienced any enlarged lymph nodes in your neck, armpits, or groin? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, and CRP.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malignancy, likely Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma or Lung Cancer, given the "B symptoms," significant weight loss, chronic cough, and recent history of incarceration which raises concern for infectious etiologies or hematologic malignancies. The previous suggestion of appendicitis is highly unlikely given the 6-month duration and lack of acute abdominal pain. Please proceed with a Chest X-Ray and Lymph Node Ultrasound.
